;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[2019–20 Western Libya offensive]]
***[[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkish]]-backed [[Government of National Accord|GNA]] forces capture the strategic [[Okba Ibn Nafa Air Base|al-Watiya airbase]] from forces loyal to [[Khalifa Haftar]], and seize a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[Pantsir missile system]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/05/libya-gna-recaptures-strategic-al-watiya-airbase-200518080809238.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.libyanexpress.com/libyas-gna-forces-seize-full-control-of-strategic-al-watiya-airbase/ (Libyan Express)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]; [[May 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**A [[car bomb]]ing at an [[intelligence agency]] installation in the central [[provinces of Afghanistan|province]] of [[Ghazni Province|Ghazni]] kills at least seven people and wounds another 40. The [[Taliban]] claims responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban-attacks/taliban-blast-near-afghan-intelligence-base-kills-seven-injures-40-idUSKBN22U18S (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 East Africa floods]]
**The [[United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs]] announces that nearly 1 million people are affected and at least 24 people have died in the flash floods that hit [[Beledweyne]] and [[Jowhar]], [[Somalia]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/nearly-1-million-people-affected-by-somalia-floods-un-1.4943847 (CTV)]
*In [[Sweden]], an earthquake with a magnitude of 4.1 strikes near [[Kiruna]]. No injuries are reported. [https://www.thelocal.se/20200518/record-earthquake-hits-mine-in-northern-sweden-kiruna (''The Local'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**In an unprecedented move, the [[World Health Organization]] holds its annual [[World Health Assembly]] using video conferencing instead of in-person meetings. [https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2020/05/17/857206256/unprecedented-world-health-assembly-convenes-online-as-pandemic-rages (NPR)]

;Law and crime
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda]]
**[[Uganda]]n police arrest [[Stella Nyanzi]], a prominent academic and vocal critic of [[President of Uganda|President]] [[Yoweri Museveni]], for inciting violence as she protested against [[lockdown]] measures taken by the [[government of Uganda|government]] to combat the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-uganda/uganda-detains-prominent-academic-protesting-coronavirus-lockdown-idUSKBN22U2JX (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**Fifteen [[pro-democracy]] activists are released on a [[HK$]]1000 bail. Notable political figures, including [[Benny Tai]], [[University of Hong Kong]] academic and one of the [[Occupy Central with Love and Peace|Occupy Central]] founders; [[Civil Human Rights Front]] convener [[Jimmy Sham]]; former Democratic Party chairwoman [[Emily Lau]]; and others, flock to the court to show support for the activists. [https://www.thestandard.com.hk/section-news/section/11/219152/15-out-on-bail-appeal-to-protest-supporters (''The Standard Hong Kong'')]
*[[2019–20 Chilean protests]]; [[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
**Protests against the [[government of Chile|government]] resume in [[Santiago]] due to food shortages in the poorest neighborhoods of the city created by the lockdown to control the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-chile/chiles-poor-clash-with-police-amid-concerns-over-food-shortages-in-outskirts-of-santiago-idUSKBN22U2YB (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of Monaco]]
**The office of [[Minister of State (Monaco)|Minister of State]] announces that [[Serge Telle]] will leave the Headship of the Monegasque government on 31 August. [https://www.lobservateurdemonaco.mc/infos/politique/serge-telle-quitte-gouvernement-monaco (''L'Observateur de Monaco'')]
